about: workflow:run-each-command-once: runs each command once on the person's own records and keeps its reply, so a retry with the same request key answers the same reply and a stale or failed command changes nothing. It replaces tools/run-each-command-once-on-the-accounts-records-keep (src/native-tool-command-receipts.mjs), whose whole job was keeping a row, its reply and its receipt in the retired record store (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Run each command once
payload.job: Run each command once on the person's own records and keep its reply: a command's change and its reply are written in one transaction with its receipt, so a retry with the same key answers the same reply without changing anything again, a key used for another request is refused, and a command that fails leaves neither a change nor a receipt.
payload.produces: The store's own objects for rows and receipts, proven on the example attempts, and each command's reply kept, repeated, refused or read back.

source.from: tools/run-each-command-once-on-the-accounts-records-keep (src/native-tool-command-receipts.mjs, moved from the old tree; the receipts helper it wraps is shared-code's native-local-command-receipts), read on the Workshop origin/main 13c05f2c8c
source.note: Only the keeping is the store's job: a row, its reply and the receipt that names the request key, in one transaction. The helper's facts about permits, generations and retained sessions were the old runtime's own form and are not carried; the intent keeps the three rules that decide an answer: the same key answers its reply, a change on a stale version is refused, and a failed command leaves nothing.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

commands.description: Commands to run this time, each {key (the request key), id, body, expected_version (optional)}, or a read {id}, or a receipt {key}

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the receipts are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form: rows (id, body, version, which rises by one with each change), and receipts (the request key, the row it changed, the body it wrote and the reply, one receipt per key). A command writes its row and its receipt in one transaction, so both are kept or neither. A command whose key has a receipt answers that receipt's reply and changes nothing when it is the same request (same id and body), and is refused when it is another request. A command with an empty key or an empty id is refused. A command with an expected_version that is not the row's current version is refused and changes nothing. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, run these in order, each through the store's own objects: [{"op": "run", "key": "k1", "id": "t1", "body": "t1 body"}, {"op": "run", "key": "k1", "id": "t1", "body": "t1 body"}, {"op": "run", "key": "k1", "id": "t2", "body": "t2 body"}, {"op": "run", "key": "k2", "id": "t2", "body": "t2 body"}, {"op": "read", "id": "t2"}, {"op": "run", "key": "k3", "id": "", "body": "x"}, {"op": "receipt", "key": "k3"}, {"op": "run", "key": "k5", "id": "t1", "body": "x", "expected_version": 0}, {"op": "read", "id": "t1"}, {"op": "receipts"}, {"op": "run", "key": "", "id": "t1", "body": "y"}]. Answers: a run gives saved (its first time), repeated (its key already has a receipt for the same request), or refused; a read gives the row's body (null when there is none); receipt gives the receipt's reply for the key, or null; receipts gives the number of receipts. Then remove the throwaway place. Submit answers: one per attempt, in order, exactly as the answers above (repeated is the word repeated; the answer of a refused run is refused).

checks.says: Each attempt gives the answer the intent says

steps.title: Keep this run's commands
steps.do: Run each item of commands through the store's own objects, in order, and read back the row each one changed. With no commands, submit empty lists. Submit answers (one per command, as in the prove step) and found_rows (each row read back, by id).

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes the receipts whose rows the person asks to erase, with their replies; a row's receipt is kept as long as the row is.
